clue.text: Was first to go after cards with rough edges

indicators.note: one piece is told to follow the other, so the cards come first in the word

parts.note: to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: Someone sorting a pack of tatty, dog-eared cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deckled paper keeps the untrimmed, feathery border left by the papermaking frame, hence its ragged margins.

clue.text: Resolve on December to March date

parts.note: the Ides of March, a date in the Roman calendar

explanation.surface: Settling on a date somewhere between December and March.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides were the middle day of the Roman month; the Ides of March, 15 March, is when Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to make up one's mind or settle a question firmly.

clue.text: Article about imitation bed covering

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

explanation.surface: A fake bedspread, described as an article in a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a fabric covering hung over a four-poster bed.

clue.text: Tends to appear faster, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone usually seems to speed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after someone is to take care of them, as a nurse tends a patient.

clue.text: The meaning of "tendency"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the gist of what is said, as in 'the ... of his argument'
second meaning: a gradual movement or trend

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style question about what a word signifies.
explanation.definitionFit: Drift is both the general gist of a speech and a gradual trend or inclination.

clue.text: Record awful lies about model in writing

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up
about means placed around, so the jumbled letters wrap the model

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of telling dreadful untruths about a fashion model in print.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Ford's famous early car, so 'model' regularly supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, a formal piece of correspondence such as those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Plant first of brassicas in high spirits

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
only the opening letter of the next word is kept

explanation.surface: A cabbage-family plant thriving in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is the spurge genus, a large group of flowering garden shrubs and succulents.

clue.text: Lie about kiss under tree

indicators.note: turned about, the letters move into a new order
in a down entry, under means the next piece is written below, so it comes after

parts.note: the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Lovers lying around kissing beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, and also names the holm oak, an evergreen.

clue.text: Used by carpenter to let rain out round a point

definitions.note: a description of the noun rather than a synonym for it

indicators.note: letting the letters out frees them to fall into a new order
round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters encircle the point

explanation.surface: A carpenter fixing a roof to stop the rain getting in around a spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, S, E and W are standard single-letter pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A treenail is a hardwood peg driven in to join timbers, a fastening a woodworker uses instead of metal.

clue.text: Alienate with row at outset

indicators.note: at the outset places that piece at the start, ahead of the rest

parts.note: read as 'set out': the three letters of set, put out of order
a line, as of hills or seats

explanation.surface: Falling out with someone after a quarrel at the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface, a quarrel, but the wordplay wants the other sense, a line. 'Outset' splits into OUT and SET, with SET put out of order and placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to drive them apart, making them unfriendly or distant towards one another.

clue.text: Is able to render part of long poem

explanation.surface: Someone capable of reciting a section of an epic.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the major divisions of a long poem, as in Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Simple mentality required for making tool

indicators.note: the phrase says the answer is made out of the run of words before it

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Only a basic intelligence is needed to fashion a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a utensil or instrument for doing a job, the same thing as a tool.

clue.text: Declaration of French attitude

parts.note: a stance or point of view

explanation.surface: A statement of the French stance on some issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposition is a sworn statement of evidence, a formal declaration made out of court.

clue.text: Girl going to and fro

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever way you travel through it

explanation.surface: A girl walking back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a common female first name, and crosswords use any girl's name for 'girl'.

clue.text: Film star silenced or otherwise mistreated

indicators.note: handled roughly and put another way, the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A movie celebrity who was gagged or badly treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen idol is a much-adored cinema actor, a celebrity of the movies.

clue.text: Company sponsorship gets strong support

explanation.surface: A corporate sponsor's money gives a project a solid foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm backing is unwavering, resolute endorsement, the same as robust or solid help.

clue.text: Traveller may take umbrage at having to act as agent

explanation.surface: A salesman annoyed at being made to work as someone's agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to speak or act on their behalf, as a proxy or delegate does.

clue.text: Player stuck round half century gets the bird …

indicators.note: stuck round means wrapped about, so the player encloses the other piece
half keeps just the front portion of the following word

parts.note: roughly the first half of the word's letters

explanation.surface: A cricketer stuck on fifty runs is out, caught by someone nicknamed the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A century in cricket is a hundred runs; a half-century is fifty, but here it is just half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The accentor is a small songbird; the hedge sparrow or dunnock is the familiar British example.

clue.text: … since batting so fast is insulting

parts.note: a batsman at the crease is in

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, scoring so quickly at the crease is rude to the bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'. The ellipsis links the surface to 16 down but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is rude and disrespectful, much like an insulting remark.

clue.text: Look attentively at Girl Guide

parts.note: short for Constance, a girl's name
a pattern used as a guide for cutting or shaping

explanation.surface: Studying a member of the Girl Guides, the youth movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl Guide' reads as one thing, a member of the Guides (the girls' scouting movement), but splits into a name and a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate something is to gaze at it thoughtfully, studying or observing it with care.

clue.text: Uncover point of chevron on sleeve

explanation.surface: Exposing the tip of a soldier's rank badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of chevron' looks like one phrase, the tip of a V, but the point is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a V-shaped band of braid on a uniform sleeve marking a non-commissioned rank.

clue.text: Three times the fool goes out to get flowers

indicators.note: going outside means one piece sits around the other

parts.note: Latin for thrice, used in prescriptions

explanation.surface: A buffoon leaves the house thrice to pick some blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Asters are daisy-like garden perennials such as Michaelmas daisies, blooming in late summer.

clue.text: School with the wrong tone

indicators.note: something wrong is not right, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: the word itself, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A school whose atmosphere is all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English public (private, fee-paying) school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a celebrated boarding establishment for boys, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Meets train as ordered where it stops

definitions.note: the phrase describes the verb's action rather than standing in for it; the train ends its run there

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new arrangement, ordered differently

explanation.surface: Someone meets a train at the station where it comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the whole clue reads as a scene in which the train ends its journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A train terminates at the final station of its route, which is where it comes to rest.

clue.text: It may measure power in some terrestrial aspect

indicators.note: the answer sits inside part of the words that follow

parts.note: letters running across the first two words

explanation.surface: A device gauging energy in some earthly feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An electricity meter is an instrument recording the energy a household consumes.

clue.text: The farm building, we hear, is an eyesore!

indicators.note: we hear means we go by how the word is said out loud

explanation.surface: A rundown pigpen spoils the view.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyesore usually means an ugly sight; here it is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, quite literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Doctor's prescription for management

definitions.meaning: first meaning: medical care given to a patient
second meaning: the way something is handled or dealt with

explanation.surface: A doctor recommends a course of action for running something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both medical care ordered for a patient and the handling or dealing with a matter.

clue.text: Go for an excursion

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a noun: energy, get-up-and-go
second meaning: an outing in a car

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb inviting you on a trip; it is the noun meaning energy or vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means both ambition or vigour and a pleasure trip taken by car.

clue.text: Pay once more for a quiet place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stand someone another round

explanation.surface: Paying a second time for a peaceful hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as RE- plus TREAT: to treat someone again.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded refuge, while re-treat means to buy someone something again.

clue.text: Waves to the birds

definitions.meaning: second meaning: colourful crow-sized birds known for tumbling display flights

explanation.surface: Someone waving at the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollers are long heavy sea swells and also a family of brightly coloured birds.
